"Migration isn't a problem to be solved." Amelia Frank-Vitale explains why deportation doesn't stop migration, what U.S. immigration policy gets wrong about Honduras, and practical fixes that would reduce harm.

Listen now: austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

Full reporting and the scoping notice PDF are here: projectsaltbox.com/p/ice-ope…
Public comments are due July 1 to DHS at the link in the piece.

Michael Wriston and Em Knepp at Project Salt Box have been doing essential, court-document-level reporting on this facility from the start. If you want to understand how ICE builds detention infrastructure, this is the work to follow.

This review exists only because a federal judge halted construction in April after finding that ICE likely failed to meet its legal environmental review obligations. The original review had been completed and approved in a single day, just one day before the purchase closed.

DHS purchased the warehouse in January for $102.4 million. The agency also awarded a renovation contract to KVG LLC of Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, valued at $113 million, with options that could bring total federal spending on the project to at least $215 million over three years.

The sewer plan runs into a state order barring any increase in sewage flow from the property, issued because the pumping station serving the site is already operating at more than 99% of its allocated capacity.

The current warehouse has 4 toilets and 800 gallons/day in municipal water. A 1,500-person facility would need 209,000 gallons/day. ICE's plan: install a 750,000-gallon on-site storage tank rather than draw from Hagerstown's system.

ICE relied on the 542-bed figure in four separate federal cases to argue that it had completed an adequate environmental review. But the new assessment now aligns with the original 1,500-bed plan that ICE previously sought to distance itself from in court.
ICE's environmental review for the Williamsport, MD warehouse describes a facility for up to 1,500 detainees, thats nearly three times the 542 it told federal courts all spring.

washingtonpost.com/politics/…

The authors conclude that when prominent media embrace conspiracy theorizing, public endorsement follows. The great replacement theory is documented as a driver of political violence against people of color and religious minorities.
More than 3 in 4 MAGA members agree immigrants 'invade and colonize' the US. Close to 6 in 10 Republicans agree. Among white Fox News viewers, 61% hold these beliefs. All white Americans = 39%.

A March 2026 poll of 1,000 Americans found 36% agree that immigrants are eroding native-born Americans' economic, political, and cultural influence. And 26% believe political elites are secretly working to replace native-born whites with immigrants.

The study tracked the same people across time. When their Fox News viewing increased, their great replacement beliefs increased with it. When it decreased, so did the beliefs. Party, ideology, and racial attitudes don't account for this.

A peer-reviewed study finds Fox News viewership independently predicts great replacement theory belief, even after controlling for partisanship, ideology, and racial attitudes. More Fox News watched means greater adoption of the conspiracy. 🧵

The Trump administration is pressuring immigrants to leave the US by cutting them off from jobs, healthcare, and housing. This includes immigrants with legal status. 

Link: www.nytimes.com/2026/05/30/u...

Full story from the Texas Tribune via KSAT:
ksat.com/news/texas/2026/05/30/ice-sued-over-inhumane-conditions-at-camp-east-montana-in-west-texas 

My Substack: austinkocher.substack.com

The camp currently holds more than 2,500 people on average and is designed to grow to 5,000 beds. TRAC data shows it has already held more detainees than any other facility in the country so far in 2026.
In March, ICE swapped out the facility's operator to improve conditions. But a letter sent to ICE last week said the situation had "continued to deteriorate", including hazardous dust exposure.

The lawsuit argues conditions amount to unconstitutional punishment and violate due process under the Fifth Amendment. One plaintiff, a man from Cameroon who fled kidnapping and torture, says he was beaten and placed in solitary for 15 days.

The camp opened in August 2025 on Fort Bliss Army base. In less than a year it has seen:
-  3 detainee deaths, including one homicide
-  A measles outbreak lasting nearly a month
-  Nearly 50 detention standards violations per ICE's own inspectors

ICE is now being sued over conditions at Camp East Montana in El Paso, it's the country's largest immigration detention facility. The lawsuit was filed Friday by the ACLU, ACLU of Texas, and the Texas Civil Rights Project.
"In at least four states, migrants detained in ICE facilities have launched hunger strikes in recent weeks to protest the conditions in which they are being held."

I'm looking for another org or two that could speak to local efforts to cut ties with an FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force. A handful of cities have done it, including Portland and Oakland. I want to know who's next! 👀 

This is for reporting @truthout.org. RTs appreciated #journorequest
